source: SRS v3.2 (frozen baseline), sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.5; design elements and test IDs from SRS Appendix B and section 4; acceptance criteria additionally bound by ADR-001..011
generated: 2026-08-18 (rev D — ADR-009 weekly window ratified; weekly cap corrected to 90 per AB 1325)

requirements.text: The system shall allow users to search for meals by location, time, hosts, or cuisine type.
requirements.designElement: Search Service, Listing Service, Google Maps Adapter

acceptanceCorrection.status: RESOLVED — criterion corrected, no code change. Option (b) of the finding was taken and is recorded here so the criterion and the implementation no longer disagree.
acceptanceCorrection.previousWording: With the Maps adapter forced to fail, a previously cached query still returns results plus a degraded-mode flag (NFR-09).
acceptanceCorrection.decision: The degraded-mode flag accompanies a stale-cache ADAPTER answer; a fresh result-page cache hit during a provider outage is a normal 200 without the flag. src/modules/search/service.js was NOT changed — its documented contract was already the correct one; the acceptance sentence was over-strict.
why: Self-contradictory as written: the sentence immediately before it requires that "a second identical query performs zero adapter calls (assert on the adapter spy)" (the NFR-01 hot-path guarantee behind the 500 ms p95 budget). A request that makes zero adapter calls cannot observe that the provider is failing, so no implementation can satisfy both halves. Reproduced probe: warm the page cache, then force maps.searchArea to reject and repeat the identical query — status 200, 1 result, adapter call count 0. There is no failure signal anywhere in the system to flag.

The SRS does not require the flag. NFR-09 and SRS §2.1.6 (Operation, degraded mode) require the system to "display an appropriate error message, use cache or previously stored data where available, and defer non-critical actions" — nothing there labels a fresh cache hit as degraded. SRS §2.5 is likewise silent. Per SPMP §1.1.2 the SRS is the frozen baseline and this inventory is a derived artifact, so the derived sentence yields.

A page-cache hit is not degraded data: the page was built from PostgreSQL (the source of truth) with a healthy geocode and lives at most SEARCH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 60 s). Flagging it would tell users a fresh answer is untrustworthy and would make the flag useless as a signal.
The genuinely degraded answers are already flagged and covered: adapter stale copy -> degraded:true and never page-cached; nothing cached -> 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED with a user-facing message.
acceptanceCorrection.rejectedAlternative: Option (a) — make the page-cache path itself report degraded — was rejected. Probing the adapter on every cache hit deletes the zero-adapter-calls guarantee in the same criterion and the p95 budget it protects, and burns free-tier quota (SRS §2.4). The only ADR-legal variant (a worker-side periodic health probe writing a Redis health marker that search reads) adds a Redis read to the hot path, spends free-tier quota on liveness polling, and still would not flag the reproduced probe, because in it the adapter is never called and never fails.
evidence: tests/tc-core/tc01-search.test.js — "with the adapter down, a previously page-cached query still returns results" (asserts 200, same ids, spy not called) and "a stale-cache adapter answer surfaces as degraded:true and the degraded page is never cached".

tests/rt-lt-resilience/rt01-wave3-degradation.test.js — RT-01 wave-3 drill 1: healthy 200 with degraded undefined; provider down -> 200 with zero adapter calls; stale area cache -> degraded:true, not cached; nothing cached -> 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED.
src/modules/search/service.js header (NFR-09 paragraph) documents the same three cases.

requirements.acceptance: GET /api/listings/search accepts any combination of {location+radiusKm, from/to datetime window, hostId, cuisine}. Against the seeded test DB: each filter alone and all four combined return exactly the expected listing IDs. Only listings with moderation_status='approved', status='active', and scheduled_start in the future are returned; a pending/rejected listing seeded in range is never returned. Address->coordinate resolution goes through the Maps adapter and the resolved coordinates + result page are written to Redis with a TTL; a second identical query performs zero adapter calls (assert on the adapter spy). With the Maps adapter forced to fail the search path still answers from cached or previously stored data (NFR-09), in three distinct cases that this criterion distinguishes: (i) a query whose RESULT PAGE is still cached is answered 200 from that page with zero adapter calls and NO degraded flag — it is an ordinary fresh cache hit (built from PostgreSQL under a healthy geocode, TTL SEARCH_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, default 60 s) and the request never consults the provider, so provider health is neither known nor knowable on that path; (ii) a query that does reach the adapter and is answered from the adapter's own STALE geocode copy returns 200 with `degraded: true`, and that degraded page is never written to the result-page cache, so recovery is visible on the next request; (iii) a location query with nothing cached anywhere returns the typed 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED carrying a user-facing message (never an unhandled 500), while non-location queries are unaffected. The degraded-mode indicator therefore accompanies a STALE-CACHE ADAPTER answer, not a fresh page-cache hit. p95 < 500 ms at 200 concurrent users in LT-01. ADR-010: search results are produced by the PUBLIC listing serializer only — coarsened coordinates (config.privacy.coarsenRadiusMeters) plus a neighbourhood/city label, never an exact street address or precise coordinates; the Redis result/geocode cache stores public precision only, so a cache hit cannot leak an exact location (asserted by reading the cached value directly).
requirements.statusNote: TC-01 + tc01-04-acceptance-gaps; TCC-03 criterion corrected, TCC-02/TCC-05 fixes unverified.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute TCC-02 (a soft-deleted host's approved listings must not stay discoverable) and TCC-05 (the page-cache existence assertion must survive >512 keys in the Redis index — full SCAN cursor loop or EXISTS, never a single-pass SCAN). Re-read the Redis result/geocode cache directly and assert public precision only (ADR-010).

requirements.text: When a user selects a meal listing, the system shall display what the dish is, the main ingredients, allergy warning, reviews, and any additional information regarding the host and meal.
requirements.acceptance: GET /api/listings/:id for an approved listing returns, in one response: name, dish description, ingredients[], allergyWarnings[], date/duration, seatCapacity, seatsRemaining, image URLs derived from object-storage keys, host summary (display name, bio, average rating, review count) and the approved reviews for that host. Assert every field is present and equals the seeded value. A listing whose moderation_status is 'pending' or 'rejected' returns 404 to any user other than its owning host (the owner sees it with its moderation status). No host email, phone, or exact street address appears in the payload (NFR-13). ADR-010: the exact street address and precise coordinates are returned only when the caller holds a booking on that listing in status pending or in progress (or is a moderator handling an FR-07 alert on it, which writes an access-log record); every other caller — including a guest whose booking is cancelled or completed — receives the public serializer output.
requirements.statusNote: TC-02; TCC-01 (host summary fallback) and TCC-04 (review preview total/cursor) claimed/observed fixed on disk, both unverified.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute TCC-01 (host summary fallback when the host row is soft-deleted or has no host_profiles row must not be host:null). TCC-04 is OPEN: the reviews array is truncated to 5 with no total and no cursor, so the FR-02 acceptance clause "the approved reviews for that host" is only partly served.

requirements.text: When a guest selects a host, the system shall show the personal page of the host, including a self-introduction, example dishes, reviews, and clear pictures of the dining location and kitchen.
requirements.acceptance: GET /api/hosts/:id returns selfIntroduction, exampleDishes (the host's approved listings), reviews about the host with numeric ratings and an average, and kitchen/dining image URLs resolved from object-storage keys. Only approved reviews and approved media are returned. The response contains no email, phone, emergency contact, or password hash for any user (assert by key allowlist). Requesting a host profile without an authenticated session returns 401 (AB-08). ADR-010: the host page shows the approximate area (coarsened coordinates + area label) for the host's listings, never the exact street address.
requirements.statusNote: TC-03 + ADR-010 public-serializer assertions.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the ADR-010 public-serializer assertions on GET /api/hosts/:id and the key-allowlist assertion (no email/phone/emergency contact/password hash), plus 401 for an unauthenticated caller (AB-08).

requirements.text: When the end of the meal is confirmed by both the host and the guest on the app, the system shall change the booking status to "completed".
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings/:id/confirm-completion sets host_confirmed or guest_confirmed depending on caller identity. After exactly one confirmation the booking status is still 'in progress' and the response reports awaiting the other party. After both confirmations status='completed' and completed_at is set. Repeating a confirmation is idempotent (no state change, 200). A user who is neither the booking's guest nor the listing's host gets 403. Confirming a booking that is 'pending' (before scheduled start) or 'cancelled' returns 409.
requirements.statusNote: TC-04 incl. concurrent dual confirmation.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute TCB-W3-02: move a listing's scheduled_start EARLIER and prove the booking.promote job is rescheduled so the booking reaches in_progress and both parties can confirm completion. Plus concurrent dual confirmation and the 403/409 branches.

requirements.text: The system shall allow both users and hosts to leave reviews for each other, including photos and a numerical rating.
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings/:id/reviews accepts {rating: integer 1..5, comment: string, imageKeys: string[]} from the guest (about the host) and from the host (about the guest). Rating outside 1..5 or non-integer returns 422. A review on a booking whose status is not 'completed' returns 409. A second review by the same author on the same booking returns 409 (at most two reviews per booking, one per direction). A created review is stored with moderation_status='pending' and is absent from GET /api/hosts/:id and GET /api/listings/:id until approved (FR-08).
requirements.statusNote: src/modules/reviews absent; endpoints answer a structured 404. Wave 4 (U4-REVIEWS).

reverification.mustProve: Not implemented. Assert absence by probe: the review endpoints answer a structured 404 and src/modules/reviews does not exist. Do not build.

requirements.text: When users have confirmed a seat for a meal, the system shall open communication for the guests and the host for any questions.
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings/:id/messages and GET /api/bookings/:id/messages succeed only for the booking's guest and the listing's host, and only while the booking status is pending, in progress, or completed; a cancelled booking returns 409 and a third party returns 403. A posted message is persisted and returned immediately (delivered), and in the SAME PostgreSQL transaction an outbox row of type 'moderation.scan' referencing the message ID is written — assert both rows exist and that no LLM adapter call occurred on the request path. Messages are never withheld pending moderation (ADR-002).
requirements.statusNote: src/modules/messaging absent. Wave 4 (U4-MESSAGING).

reverification.mustProve: Not implemented. Assert absence by probe. Do not build.

requirements.text: When a user submits a safety alert, the system shall persist the alert, notify the moderator, and attempt delivery to the user's approved emergency-contact channel (email via SendGrid in v1.0); failed delivery shall be retried and remain visible for review.
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings/:id/safety-alerts persists a SAFETY_ALERT row (booking_id, raising_user_id, delivery_status='pending') and an outbox row in one transaction, and returns 201 within the request without calling SendGrid inline. The worker then (a) creates a moderator-queue entry, (b) sends the emergency-contact email through the SendGrid adapter, (c) sets delivery_status='delivered'. With an injected SendGrid failure, delivery_status becomes 'retrying', attempts increment with exponential backoff, the alert remains listed in GET /api/moderation/alerts, and after max attempts it is dead-lettered but still visible. If the raising user has no emergency contact, the moderator notification still succeeds and delivery_status='no_channel'. ADR-011: delivery is email via the SendGrid adapter; in dev and the whole automated suite both notification adapters resolve to the mock transport, and each attempt writes a NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT row (recipient, channel, status) that the test asserts on instead of asserting on SendGrid's behaviour. WAVE-3 CLOSE-OUT NOTE (2026-08-17, rev D — supersedes the rev-C note): src/modules/safety/{repo,service,routes}.js, src/schemas/safety.js and src/outbox/handlers/safetyAlert.js landed in repair round 1 (f7f954c) together with tests/unit/safety.test.js, tests/tc-core/tc07-safety.test.js and tests/it-adapters/it04-safety-delivery.test.js, and have now been independently RE-EXECUTED against the tree at bc27199 (git diff f7f954c..bc27199 -- src/ is empty, so the module under test is byte-identical to the one that landed). CORRECTION: the rev-C note claimed the moderator-queue clause (GET /api/moderation/alerts) was 'owned by U4-MODERATION and does not exist yet'. That was false at f7f954c and is false now — src/modules/safety/routes.js declares router.get('/moderation/alerts', requireSession, validate({query: safetySchemas.alertQueueQuery}), ...), src/routes/index.js KNOWN_MODULES mounts it, and the route was executed: 401 unauthenticated, 403 for an ordinary session, 200 listing the alert for a roles:['user','moderator'] session, with the ?status filter and the pageSize cap enforced (tests/tc-core/tc07-safety.test.js). The 'remain visible for review' clause was proved to its terminal state: once the retry budget is exhausted the outbox job is 'dead' with attempt_count = config.outbox.maxAttempts (8) and the alert is 'failed', yet it is still returned by the queue. SCOPE BOUNDARY — this is the FR-07 SAFETY-ALERT queue over safety_alerts. It is deliberately NOT the FR-08 moderation queue (moderation_queue, content_type in listing/review/message), which has no implementing code and remains wave 4; nothing in this entry may be read as FR-08 content moderation being done.
requirements.statusNote: RE-VERIFIED at bc27199 (rev D): every acceptance clause was executed and passed — TC-07 (tests/tc-core/tc07-safety.test.js), IT-04 (tests/it-adapters/it04-safety-delivery.test.js), the IT-F2 block of tests/it-adapters/it-w3rv-reverify.test.js and the 'RE-VERIFY FR-07' block of tests/tc-core/tcc-w3-reverify.test.js: 201 with zero notification_attempts rows written on the request path, alert + outbox row in one transaction with an IDs-only payload, worker delivery to moderator + emergency contact (safety-alert-emergency:sent, safety-alert-moderator:sent) then delivery_status='delivered', no_channel when the raiser has no contact on file, and injected-failure -> 'retrying' -> backoff -> job 'dead' at attempt_count 8 with the alert 'failed' and STILL listed in GET /api/moderation/alerts. Corrects rev C, which recorded 'partial' on the false premise that the moderator-queue route was wave 4; statusAt_f7f954c is likewise corrected to met_pending_reverify because src/ is unchanged between f7f954c and bc27199.

reverification.mustProve: DONE (2026-08-17, finding TCC-RV-03). Re-executed end to end against the module that landed in f7f954c: 201 with no inline SendGrid call, worker delivers the emergency-contact email through the ADR-011 mock transport, NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT rows exist, an injected failure produces retrying -> backoff -> dead-letter while the alert stays visible in the queue, and no_channel when the raiser has no emergency contact. The moderator-queue route GET /api/moderation/alerts named in the criterion DOES exist (src/modules/safety/routes.js, mounted by src/routes/index.js) and was exercised for 401/403/200, the status filter and the pageSize cap — the rev-C claim that it was wave 4 was wrong. Not to be confused with the FR-08 moderation queue over listing/review/message content, which is still wave 4 and not implemented.

requirements.text: When user-generated content is submitted, the system shall apply the deterministic pre-filter and automated moderation flow, route flagged or low-confidence content to human review, and enforce the publication policy: public content (listings, reviews) remains pending until it passes moderation; private messages are delivered and scanned asynchronously; a moderation-provider outage keeps public content pending rather than publishing it unreviewed.
requirements.designElement: Moderation Module (pre-filter, LLM, human review, publication policy)
requirements.acceptance: Every listing, review, and message submission runs the deterministic pre-filter (blocklist, regex, per-user submission rate limit) before any LLM call; a blocklist hit yields moderation_status='rejected' with decided_by='pre-filter' and zero LLM adapter calls. Content passing the pre-filter is scanned by the worker via the LLM adapter, which returns {category, confidence}; confidence below MODERATION_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD or any flagged category creates a moderator-queue item and leaves public content pending. Approved public content becomes visible only after moderation_status='approved'. Messages are readable immediately regardless of scan state; a message later flagged is hidden and queued. With the LLM adapter forced to fail for all attempts, listings and reviews stay 'pending' indefinitely (assert they never appear in search/detail) while the job is retried. Every outcome writes a MODERATION_DECISION row with category, outcome, decided_by in {pre-filter, llm, human}. ADR-007: the LLM stage is reached only through the provider-agnostic adapter configured by LLM_MODERATION_BASE_URL / LLM_MODERATION_API_KEY / MODERATION_MODEL (Google Gemini free tier is the configured v1.0 provider); no provider name, model id or key is hardcoded, CI and the automated suite run the deterministic mock adapter, and only the IT-03 measurement run may call the live API.
requirements.statusNote: No pre-filter, no LLM stage, no moderation.scan handler, no decision table writer. Wave 4 (U4-MODERATION). Wave-3 enqueues moderation.scan jobs that dead-letter, so public content stays pending — FR-08's required failure direction.

reverification.mustProve: Not implemented. Prove only the safe failure direction: an unhandled moderation.scan job dead-letters and public content stays PENDING and invisible. No NFR-10 number may be quoted.

requirements.text: While a user does not satisfy the eligibility policy for an action (canReserveSeat for reserving a seat; canPublishListing for creating a listing — NFR-06), the system shall restrict that action.
requirements.acceptance: State-driven, both states asserted. Restricted: a user missing email verification, full name, or phone gets 403 with reason codes from POST /api/bookings; a user missing a completed host profile or host-agreement acceptance gets 403 from POST /api/listings. Permitted: once the missing attributes are set, the identical request succeeds. Both checks are served by the single exported policy module (canReserveSeat / canPublishListing); a repository-wide grep proves no other module re-implements either predicate (ADR-006).
requirements.statusNote: TC-09 both states + single-policy grep.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the both-states truth table and the repository-wide grep proving one policy module. Additionally prove the FR-10 consequence chain: after verifying through the DELIVERED link, canReserveSeat flips to true.

requirements.text: When a person submits valid registration data, the system shall create an unverified account and send an email-verification request; only successful token confirmation shall mark the email as verified.
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/auth/register with valid data creates a USER row with email_verified=false, an Argon2id/bcrypt password hash (never the plaintext), and, in the same transaction, an outbox row of type 'email.verification' carrying only IDs. A duplicate email returns 409 (unique constraint, AB-07). GET/POST /api/auth/verify-email with the correct single-use token sets email_verified=true and consumes the token; a wrong, already-used, or expired (> EMAIL_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS) token returns 400 and leaves email_verified=false. No email adapter call occurs on the request path. FR-10 DELIVERY PROOF — added 2026-08-15 after finding TCB-W3-01, the wave-3 blocker. The token used to verify MUST be the value actually DELIVERED to the recipient, read out of the ADR-011 mock transport's recorded delivery (render context / message body), NEVER out of the in-process return value of registration or of the token-minting function. Executable form: POST /api/auth/register -> run the outbox worker until the 'email.verification' job is drained -> read the recorded delivery for that user -> extract the verification URL/token from it -> submit exactly that extracted value to the verify endpoint -> re-read the USER row and assert email_verified=true AND that the user now passes canReserveSeat (NFR-06). Assert additionally that no persisted artefact (outbox payload, notification_attempt row, users row, log line) contains the usable raw token (ADR-003 IDs-only), and that a retry/redelivery of the same job neither mints a credential that is not mailed nor invalidates a link already mailed. A test that reads the token from a function return value does NOT verify FR-10: waves 1-2 reported FR-10 as PASS on exactly that mistake while the delivered email carried only a SHA-256 digest, so no real user could ever verify an email and therefore no real user could ever become eligible to book or publish.

acceptanceCorrection.status: OPEN UNTIL RE-VERIFIED — the fix landed in repair round 1 (f7f954c, worker-side resolveRenderContext in src/outbox/handlers/emailVerification.js). It is a fixer claim plus a green suite; the wave-3 close-out run must reproduce the ORIGINAL failure scenario and show it no longer reproduces.
acceptanceCorrection.why: The criterion as written before this revision could be satisfied by a test that never looked at the delivered email, which is how a production-blocking defect passed two waves of verification. The criterion now names the observation point, not just the outcome.

requirements.statusNote: BLOCKER TCB-W3-01 fixed in repair round 1. Highest-priority re-verification: prove verification end to end from the DELIVERED email.

reverification.mustProve: HIGHEST PRIORITY. Prove end to end that the value the ADR-011 mock transport actually DELIVERED (render context / message body) verifies the account: register -> drain the outbox -> read the recorded delivery -> extract the link/token -> submit exactly that value -> users.email_verified = true. A token taken from an in-process return value proves nothing (this is exactly how waves 1-2 mis-reported FR-10 as PASS). Also re-assert ADR-003: no persisted artefact carries the usable raw token.

requirements.text: When an eligible host submits complete listing data, the system shall create, update, or cancel the listing while enforcing the configured one-listing-per-host-per-day and meal/seat limits (AB 626).
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/listings by a canPublishListing-eligible host creates a listing with moderation_status='pending'. A second listing by the same host whose scheduled date (in the configured locale timezone) equals an existing non-cancelled listing's date returns 409 MEHKO_DAILY_LISTING_LIMIT — enforced by a DB unique index on (host_id, local_date) so concurrent duplicate creations cannot both commit. seatCapacity greater than config.mehko.maxMealsPerDay (default 30 per AB 626) returns 422. The configured weekly cap (default 90 meals per host per week — AB 626 as amended by AB 1325) is enforced by that same single server-side check, summed over a fixed Monday-Sunday America/Los_Angeles calendar week. That window shape was ratified by the team on 2026-08-18 (ADR-009 §'Weekly window shape — RATIFIED 2026-08-18'; see the specDecision block above), on the basis that California MEHKO weekly limits are calculated on a standard calendar-week basis rather than a rolling-day one. A calendar week is by construction spreadable across its boundary — filling Saturday and Sunday of one week and Monday and Tuesday of the next places twice the weekly cap inside a single 7-day span — which is an accepted residual risk following from the statute's own basis, not a defect; the stricter rolling 7-day window is retained in ADR-009 as a ready-made recipe should a county or another jurisdiction require it. A TC-11 pass is therefore evidence against a RATIFIED requirement and may be cited as AB 626 / AB 1325 weekly-compliance evidence. PATCH updates and POST /api/listings/:id/cancel work only for the owning host (403 otherwise); a material content edit resets moderation_status to 'pending'. Cancelling a listing with active bookings cancels them and enqueues notifications (FR-13). ADR-009: the caps come from src/config (California v1.0: 1 listing/host/day, 30 meals/host/day, 90 meals/host/week) and are never inline in the service; day and week boundaries are evaluated in America/Los_Angeles, not UTC and not the caller's timezone (a submission at 23:30 PT and one at 00:30 PT the next day are different days; the same two instants are the same UTC day). Exactly one server-side enforcement point is consulted by create, update and cancel/re-create paths.
requirements.statusNote: Daily cap, single enforcement point and LA-timezone boundaries met (TC-11). The WEEKLY window shape is an unratified spec ambiguity (TCB-W3-05 / ADR-009 open sub-decision) — no AB 626 weekly-compliance claim may rest on a TC-11 pass.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute MTUT-W3-01 / COV-05 / TCB-W3-06: the listing audit record must carry the YYYY-MM-DD America/Los_Angeles calendar day, not a stringified JS Date. The daily cap, single enforcement point and LA-timezone boundaries are re-executed. The WEEKLY window shape stays an unratified ADR-009 sub-decision (TCB-W3-05): report it, do not pick a reading, and make no AB 626 weekly-compliance claim from a TC-11 pass.

specDecision.status: RESOLVED — ratified by the team 2026-08-18. Recorded in ADR-009 §"Weekly window shape — RATIFIED 2026-08-18" and its Amendment log. No longer an open question.
specDecision.question: The FR-11 weekly cap (90 meals per host per week, AB 1325) is summed over WHICH window — the Monday-anchored America/Los_Angeles calendar week that src/modules/listings/mehko.js weekRangeFor() implements, or a rolling 7-day window?
specDecision.decision: A fixed Monday–Sunday America/Los_Angeles calendar week. California MEHKO weekly limits are calculated on a standard calendar-week basis, not a rolling-day basis; state operational standards treat the week as a fixed 7-day calendar block, with county health departments enforcing precise tracking. src/modules/listings/mehko.js weekRangeFor() already implemented this reading, so no code change was needed for the window shape.
specDecision.capCorrection: Ratification also corrected the weekly cap from 60 to 90 meals: AB 626 set 60, Assembly Bill 1325 raised it to 90. The former value was over-restrictive (it refused listings a host is legally entitled to post), so it created no compliance exposure, but it was wrong. Changed in src/config/locale.js plus the six assertions that pinned 60.
specDecision.acceptedResidualRisk: A calendar week is by construction spreadable across its boundary: filling Sat+Sun of one week and Mon+Tue of the next places twice the weekly cap inside a single 7-day span. This follows from the statute’s own calendar-week basis and is accepted, not a defect.
specDecision.cdrConsequence: A TC-11 pass is now evidence against a RATIFIED requirement, so the FR-11 weekly clause may be cited as AB 626 / AB 1325 weekly-compliance evidence. Before 2026-08-18 it could not.

requirements.text: When an eligible guest requests a seat on a listing with remaining capacity, the system shall atomically create the booking and reduce available capacity; otherwise, it shall reject the request without changing capacity. A configurable per-guest limit on concurrent pending bookings shall be enforced.
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings inserts the BOOKING row and decrements listings.seats_remaining in ONE PostgreSQL transaction using a conditional UPDATE (`SET seats_remaining = seats_remaining - 1 WHERE id = $1 AND seats_remaining > 0`) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. With seats_remaining=1 and N=50 concurrent requests, exactly 1 booking is created, seats_remaining=0, and the other 49 receive 409 with capacity unchanged (LT-01 race test asserts sum(bookings)=capacity, never overbooked). A guest already holding config.booking.maxConcurrentPending (default 3) pending bookings receives 409 BOOKING_LIMIT (AB-02). An ineligible guest receives 403 (FR-09) and no row is written. A booking on one's own listing returns 409.
requirements.statusNote: TC-12 + LT-01 race (50 concurrent on 1 seat).

reverification.mustProve: The 40-concurrent-guest race assertion (3x201 / 37x409 / seats 0) must produce the same result on 5 consecutive full-suite runs. Fix the cause of any variance (connection-pool saturation, shared-state assertion), never by retries, sleeps or a weakened assertion.

requirements.text: When a booking is created, cancelled, or changes status, the system shall enqueue the configured notification to affected users; notification-provider failure shall not roll back or delay the booking transaction.
requirements.acceptance: Every booking create/cancel/status transition writes exactly one outbox row per affected recipient in the SAME transaction as the booking row (assert both committed or neither, by forcing a post-insert error and observing zero rows of both). Outbox payloads contain IDs only — a test asserts no email address, phone number, or name appears in any payload JSON (ADR-003). With the SendGrid and FCM adapters forced to throw, POST /api/bookings still returns 201 in under 500 ms and the booking is committed. The worker records a NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT per try with status in {sent, failed, retrying}, retries with exponential backoff up to config.outbox.maxAttempts, and dead-letters afterwards. RT-02: after a simulated worker crash mid-job the job is re-claimed and delivered exactly once per recipient (idempotency key asserted). ADR-011: the configured channel is email via SendGrid; the FCM adapter exists but is gated behind notifications.push.enabled which defaults to false (asserted from config), and dev/test resolve both adapters to the mock transport that records NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPT rows. Both adapters are worker-only: a test asserts no file under src/modules/**/routes.js or service.js imports src/adapters/*.
requirements.statusNote: TC-13 + RT-02; TCB-W3-03 (no notification on pending->in_progress) and TCB-W3-04 (missing SendGrid template ids) fixed in repair round 1, unverified.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute TCB-W3-03 (pending -> in_progress must enqueue a notification), TCB-W3-04 (every template id emitted by an outbox handler exists in the SendGrid subject registry — assert the registry lookup, not just a send), IT-F4 (neither SendGrid nor FCM can reach a live provider under NODE_ENV=test) and COV-03 (lifecycle.isLivePendingJob's decisive branch is actually executed).

requirements.text: When a guest or host cancels a booking before the listing's scheduled start, the system shall set the booking to cancelled, atomically restore the seat capacity, and notify the affected parties (FR-13).
requirements.acceptance: POST /api/bookings/:id/cancel by the guest or the listing's host before scheduled_start sets status='cancelled', increments listings.seats_remaining by exactly 1, and writes the notification outbox rows — all in one transaction. seats_remaining never exceeds seat_capacity (asserted after repeated/concurrent cancel attempts; a second cancel is idempotent and does not double-restore). Cancelling at or after scheduled_start returns 409. A non-participant returns 403.
requirements.statusNote: TC-14 incl. idempotent double-cancel.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute cancel -> atomic seat restore -> notification outbox rows, idempotent double-cancel, and seats_remaining never exceeding seat_capacity under concurrent cancels.

requirements.text: REST API shall deliver 95th-percentile response time under 500ms for core operations (e.g., browse listings, search, review), sustaining up to 200 concurrent users.
requirements.acceptance: k6 scenario at 200 concurrent virtual users for >= 5 minutes against production-like seed volumes exercising GET /api/listings/search, GET /api/listings/:id, GET /api/hosts/:id and GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews reports http_req_duration p(95) < 500 ms with error rate < 1%. The measured p95 number is recorded in the run report; a run that cannot reach 200 VUs on the host machine must report the achieved level and be marked untestable rather than passed.
requirements.statusNote: Measured p95 253.7 ms at 200 VUs over 791,709 requests, 0 errors, against NFR-02 volumes — but the harness is a Node loopback VU loop, not k6 (RTLT-02). Evidence, not a pass, until wave 7 re-runs under k6.

reverification.mustProve: k6 is not installed on this host, so the instrument the criterion names cannot be run. Report the existing Node-loopback measurement (p95 253.7 ms at 200 VUs over 791,709 requests, 0 errors) as EVIDENCE, explicitly not as a pass, and record RTLT-02 as untestable here. Do not vendor k6.

requirements.text: The system shall support at least 10,000 registered users and 1,000 active dinner listings/bookings per day while continuing to meet the NFR-01 latency targets.
requirements.acceptance: The volume seed loads >= 10,000 users, >= 1,000 listings for a single day and >= 1,000 bookings for that day. With that dataset present, the LT-01 scenario is re-run and still reports p(95) < 500 ms. EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the search query shows index usage (no sequential scan on listings) and required indexes exist on (scheduled_start), (host_id, local_date), (moderation_status), and the geo/cuisine filter columns.
requirements.statusNote: Volume dataset (10,000 users / 1,000 listings / 1,000 bookings / 1,001 reviews) loads and LT-01 still meets the budget; same k6 caveat as NFR-01.

reverification.mustProve: Same k6 caveat. The volume dataset (10,000 users / 1,000 listings / 1,000 bookings) loads and the latency budget still holds under the substitute harness; index usage must be re-asserted by EXPLAIN if claimed.

requirements.text: All network transit across mobile, web, and backend services must strictly enforce HTTPS/TLS 1.2 or higher.
requirements.acceptance: The HTTPS server is created with minVersion 'TLSv1.2' (configuration review asserts the literal option). A plain-HTTP request to the service is refused with 403/426 and an 'HTTPS required' body — never served content and never 200. HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security, max-age >= 15552000) is present on every response. A TLS scan of the running dev server negotiates TLS 1.2/1.3 only and fails for TLS 1.0/1.1. Test-mode transport relaxation is gated behind an explicit config flag that fails closed when NODE_ENV=production.
requirements.statusNote: ST-01 against a real https.Server: cleartext refused, TLS 1.0/1.1 refused, 1.2/1.3 accepted, HSTS present.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute ST-01 against a real https.Server started through src/server.js: cleartext refused, TLS 1.0/1.1 refused, 1.2/1.3 accepted, HSTS present.

requirements.text: User passwords shall be stored using an industry-standard hashing algorithm (e.g., Argon2id, bcrypt). No plain text password shall be stored.
requirements.acceptance: users.password_hash matches the Argon2id ($argon2id$) or bcrypt ($2b$) format with documented parameters (Argon2id memoryCost >= 19456 KiB, timeCost >= 2; or bcrypt cost >= 12). Registering then querying the DB shows the plaintext appears in no column. A grep over the whole repository proves no logger, error handler, or response serializer emits the password field (the request validation layer redacts it). Two registrations with the same password produce different hashes (per-user salt).
requirements.statusNote: ST-02: Argon2id parameters, no plaintext column, redaction proven by execution.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute ST-02: Argon2id parameters, no plaintext in any column, redaction proven by executing the logger and the validator rather than by grep alone.

requirements.text: Login attempts shall be rate-limited or temporarily locked after 5 failed attempts within 10 minutes to prevent brute-force attacks.
requirements.acceptance: Five failed POST /api/auth/login attempts for the same account within a 10-minute sliding window cause the 6th attempt to return 429 with Retry-After, even when the credentials are correct. The counter is stored in Redis keyed by account and by source IP with a 600-second TTL. After the lockout window elapses (clock advanced in test) a correct login succeeds. A successful login resets the counter. ST-03 scripts the full sequence and asserts the exact 5-in-10-minutes boundary (attempt 5 fails as invalid credentials, attempt 6 is locked out).
requirements.statusNote: ST-03: 5-in-10-minutes boundary, per-account and per-source-IP counters.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute ST-03: the exact 5-in-10-minutes boundary (attempt 5 invalid, attempt 6 locked out with Retry-After), per-account AND per-source-IP counters, reset on success.

requirements.text: When a user registers or updates their profile, the system shall validate email verification and evaluate action-specific eligibility policies: canReserveSeat requires a verified email, full name, and phone number; canPublishListing additionally requires a completed host profile and host-agreement acceptance. Actions for which the user is ineligible are restricted (FR-09). The policies sit behind one interface, so v2.0 identity verification can replace the internal rules.
requirements.acceptance: A single module exports evaluate(userId, action) plus canReserveSeat and canPublishListing and is the only place those rules exist. Truth-table test: canReserveSeat is true only when email_verified AND full_name AND phone_number are all present; canPublishListing additionally requires host_profile_complete AND host_agreement_accepted_at. Each false case returns machine-readable reason codes. Registration and profile update recompute and persist the eligibility flags on the USER row, and the flags equal the policy result after every mutation.
requirements.statusNote: IT-02 truth table + persisted-flag equality after every mutation.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the IT-02 truth table and the persisted-flag equality after every mutation, and prove the flags recompute after email verification through the delivered link.

requirements.text: Key interfaces shall follow WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines.
requirements.acceptance: An automated axe-core audit over the key React interfaces (search/browse, listing detail, host profile, booking flow, signup/login, messaging, moderator queue) reports zero violations of impact 'serious' or 'critical' against the wcag2a/wcag2aa rule sets. Keyboard-only traversal reaches every interactive control with a visible focus indicator; all images carry alt text; form controls have associated labels and errors are announced via aria-live; colour contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text. The 5-participant moderated usability study is a human activity recorded as such.
requirements.statusNote: client/ does not exist; no .jsx/.tsx anywhere in the repo; npm run test:a11y fails on purpose so its presence is never read as coverage. Waves 5-6 + U7-A11Y-UX.

reverification.mustProve: Not implemented: client/ does not exist and no .jsx/.tsx file exists in the repository. npm run test:a11y fails on purpose so its presence is never read as coverage. The 5-participant study is a human activity.

requirements.text: Important actions (ex., user registrations, booking, cancellation) shall be logged. The system shall also log and monitor errors; records shall be sufficient for developers to identify the cause.
requirements.acceptance: Performing registration, booking creation, booking cancellation, and a moderation decision in a test environment produces one structured JSON audit record each, containing event name, correlation/request ID, actor user ID, subject entity ID, outcome, and timestamp. Every request carries a correlation ID that propagates into the outbox payload and into the worker's log lines for the resulting job (assert the same ID appears on both sides). Errors log message, stack, correlation ID and HTTP status. Logs contain user IDs only — a scan of captured log output finds no email address, phone number, name, or password (SRS §3.4 PII register).
requirements.statusNote: MT-01 verified for real, minus the moderation-decision action, which is not performable until FR-08 ships. MTUT-W3-01/02 and COV-05 fixes unverified.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute MT-01 for registration, booking create/cancel/complete/promote and media attach/delete: one structured record each with event, correlation ID, actor, subject, outcome, timestamp; correlation ID propagating into the outbox row and back out on the worker line; MTUT-W3-02 (the worker-initiated booking.promoted record must name an actor); and the PII sweep over two captured corpora. The moderation-decision action remains unperformable (FR-08 is wave 4).

requirements.text: During the demo period, the system shall maintain 99% availability. If an external service (e.g., Google Maps, SendGrid, or Firebase Cloud Messaging) becomes unavailable, the system shall display an appropriate error message, use cache or previously stored data where available, and defer non-critical actions such as notifications or moderation requests until the external service becomes available again.
requirements.acceptance: Each adapter (Maps, SendGrid, FCM, LLM, object storage) enforces a timeout (default 3000 ms), bounded retries with exponential backoff, and a documented fallback. RT-01 cuts off each service in turn: with Maps down, search returns cached results and a degraded-mode indicator plus a user-facing message; with SendGrid or FCM down, bookings still commit and notification jobs remain queued and are delivered after recovery; with the LLM down, public content stays 'pending' and messages still deliver; with object storage down, listing detail renders with a placeholder rather than a 500. No unhandled 5xx is returned in any drill, and every deferred job completes once the service is restored. The LLM adapter's degraded path is exercised against the mock (ADR-007), not the live provider; RT-01 asserts that a Google-side failure degrading both Maps (ADR-005) and moderation (ADR-007) at once still leaves bookings committable and public content pending.
requirements.statusNote: RT-01 drills per adapter; the LLM-outage drill asserts public content stays pending.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the RT-01 per-adapter outage drills including the ADR-002 property that a moderation outage leaves public content PENDING, and the three distinct FR-01 degraded cases the corrected TCC-03 criterion distinguishes.

requirements.text: The AI assistance used to detect and reduce spam, fraudulent activity, abusive language, and inappropriate content must operate with false positive and false negative rates of less than 5%.
requirements.acceptance: A versioned labelled evaluation set of at least 200 items (offensive, spam, fraudulent and benign in balanced proportions, checked into tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/vN/) is scored end-to-end through the real pipeline (pre-filter then LLM). The harness prints and asserts falsePositiveRate < 0.05 and falseNegativeRate < 0.05 and fails if the set contains fewer than 200 items. Results (set version, model/prompt version, counts, both rates) are written to a versioned results file so the bound can be re-checked when the model or prompt changes. ADR-008: the evaluation set is synthetic and team-authored (never scraped), balanced across offensive/spam/fraudulent/benign, at least 200 items, versioned as a directory under tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/vN/. NO PASS MAY BE CLAIMED without a recorded human label sign-off (reviewer name, date, set version) in the results file alongside the model id and prompt version (ADR-007); a run against an unreviewed set reports provisional numbers and does not close NFR-10. STATE AT 2026-08-15: the ADR-008 set now EXISTS — tests/fixtures/moderation-eval/v1/ carries 224 synthetic items (56 offensive / 56 spam / 56 fraudulent / 56 benign) with a manifest declaring provenance, metric definitions and a set-integrity test. The rest of NFR-10 does not: there is no pre-filter, no LLM classification stage, no moderation.scan handler, no results file and no human label sign-off, so nothing can be scored and NO NUMBER MAY BE QUOTED. Scoring the set through the ADR-007 deterministic MOCK adapter is explicitly NOT a measurement (the mock is a fixture-pattern matcher that scores unseen abusive text as benign at 0.99 confidence) and must never be reported as an NFR-10 result.
requirements.statusNote: Eval set exists (224 synthetic items); pipeline, run, results file and human sign-off do not. Unmeasurable, and no number may be quoted (IT-F1).

reverification.mustProve: Unmeasurable in this tree. The ADR-008 v1 set exists (224 synthetic items) but there is no pre-filter, no LLM stage, no moderation.scan handler, no results file and no human label sign-off. NO NUMBER MAY BE QUOTED, and scoring the set through the deterministic mock adapter is not a measurement (IT-F1).

requirements.text: The system shall validate and sanitize all user inputs to prevent SQL injections, cross-site scripting (XSS), and other injection attacks.
requirements.acceptance: Every route declares a schema (body, query, params) enforced by one shared validation middleware; a test enumerates the router and fails if any route lacks a schema. Unknown properties are stripped and type/length/range violations return 422 with field-level errors and no stack trace. All SQL is parameterized — a repository grep proves no string-concatenated or template-literal-interpolated SQL exists. ST-04 fires SQLi payloads (e.g. `' OR 1=1 --`, `'; DROP TABLE users; --`) and XSS payloads (e.g. ``, ``) at every input boundary (search, listing text, chat, reviews, profile) and asserts: no 500, no data leakage, tables intact, and stored/returned text is escaped or sanitized so no executable markup survives.
requirements.statusNote: ST-04 payload suite at every wave-0..3 boundary + parameterized-SQL grep; the last raw SQL in a route file (W3-ADR-04/COV-07) is the open exception.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the ST-04 payload suite at every wave-0..3 boundary and the parameterized-SQL grep. The ST-04 media contentType/kind assertion must become deterministic (it counts rows in the whole media_objects table). W3-ADR-04 / COV-07: the raw SELECT in src/modules/media/routes.js:81 moves into the media repo so no DB access remains in the route layer.

requirements.text: Users shall be able to delete their account from the application. Upon deletion, all personal data (name, email, phone number, pictures) shall be erased or irreversibly anonymized within 30 days; reviews may be retained in anonymized form. Personal data of accounts inactive for 24 months shall be deleted after notice. Database backups containing deleted data shall expire within 30 days.
requirements.acceptance: DELETE /api/users/me marks the account deleted and enqueues an erasure job with a due date of now + config.privacy.erasureDays (30). Running the lifecycle job erases or irreversibly anonymizes name, email, phone, emergency contact and password hash on the USER row, deletes every media object owned by the user from object storage by key via the media adapter (assert delete-by-key called per key and that a subsequent fetch 404s), and rewrites reviews, bookings and safety alerts to anonymized author references while retaining them. ST-05 asserts a full-database scan finds none of the user's PII strings after the job, and that the backup-retention configuration/script expires backups older than 30 days. An inactivity sweep flags accounts with last_active_at older than 24 months, records the notice, and erases after the notice period.
requirements.statusNote: No deletion endpoint, no erasure/anonymisation job, no backup-expiry configuration (STS-W3-03). The media delete-by-key primitive works end to end against MinIO, which is the substrate only. Wave 4 (U4-PRIVACY).

reverification.mustProve: Not implemented: no deletion endpoint, no erasure/anonymisation job, no backup-expiry configuration (STS-W3-03). The media delete-by-key primitive works against MinIO but nothing in src/ calls it. Report not_implemented with evidence; do not build wave 4.

requirements.text: The system shall collect only the personal data enumerated in section 3.4 (data minimization). Personal data shall be encrypted in transit (NFR-03) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent); access shall be role-restricted and logged. On request, users shall receive a copy of their personal data within 30 days, consistent with CCPA obligations. Emergency-contact details are a third party's personal data: collected minimally (name, phone, email), used only for FR-07 alerts, and included in the registering user's deletion scope.
requirements.acceptance: A schema test asserts the USER/emergency-contact columns are exactly the SRS §3.4 set — no extra personal attribute is stored, and API responses are built from explicit field allowlists. Phone number and emergency-contact fields are stored encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a key from the environment (the ciphertext in the column is not the plaintext; decryption round-trips), and the deployment note documents volume/disk encryption for the rest. Personal-data reads by a Moderator/admin role are permitted only for that role (403 otherwise) and each such read writes an access-log record with actor, subject and purpose. POST /api/users/me/export produces a machine-readable copy of every PII class in the §3.4 register for the requesting user within the 30-day SLA (job created immediately, due date asserted), and the export contains that user's data only. ADR-007 open action: before any real user content is sent to the moderation provider, the team records a finding on the provider's current free-tier data-use terms as part of ST-06 (the pipeline scans private messages, and the SRS §3.4 PII register lists the LLM API as an external recipient).
requirements.statusNote: Data minimisation, field-level AES-256-GCM at rest and allowlist serialisation are proven; the CCPA export path does not exist (STS-W3-03) and two ST-06 documentation clauses are only partly closed. Wave 4 (U4-PRIVACY).

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute STS-W3-02 (production config must refuse the committed sample FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the minioadmin credentials), STS-W3-01 (serializeUser must not 500 the owner on a non-canonical *_enc column) and STS-W3-05 (the two ST-06 documentation clauses). The CCPA export path still does not exist, so NFR-13 stays PARTIAL.

requirements.text: Fake host / fake listing: an attacker creates a host account with fabricated identity and stolen photos to collect bookings or lure guests to an unsafe location.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Eligibility Policy Service, Moderation Module, Review Service, Safety Alert Service
requirements.acceptance: A host account that has not completed the profile/host-agreement gate cannot publish (403, FR-09/NFR-06). Every created listing enters moderation_status='pending' and is invisible in search until approved (FR-08); a listing flagged by the pipeline is routed to the moderator queue and never published. Mutual reviews are attributable to completed bookings only (FR-05) and the safety-alert path is reachable from an active booking (FR-07). The test asserts an unapproved/unverified host's listing never appears in GET /api/listings/search.
requirements.statusNote: Eligibility gate and pending-until-approved hold; the moderation half (FR-08) and mutual reviews (FR-05) are wave 4.

reverification.mustProve: The eligibility gate and pending-until-approved invisibility are re-executed; the moderation half (FR-08) and mutual reviews (FR-05) are wave 4, so AB-01 stays PARTIAL.

requirements.text: Fraudulent / hoarding bookings: a user mass-reserves seats they never intend to use, blocking real guests and wasting host effort.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Eligibility Policy Service, Booking Service, Logging
requirements.acceptance: A scripted guest attempting 20 sequential bookings is stopped at config.booking.maxConcurrentPending (default 3) with 409 BOOKING_LIMIT; the 4th onward create no rows and leave seats_remaining unchanged. Ineligible users are blocked before any capacity check (FR-09). Every create/cancel writes an audit record with actor and booking IDs so the pattern is reconstructable (NFR-08). Concurrent hoarding attempts never overbook (FR-12 race assertion).
requirements.statusNote: Per-guest pending-booking cap + race assertions.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the per-guest concurrent-pending cap sequentially AND under concurrency, and the never-overbook race assertion.

requirements.text: Spam or scripted listings: bots create listings at scale to advertise or phish.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Listing Service (MEHKO invariant), Moderation Module, Input Validation, Auth rate limiting
requirements.acceptance: A script creating 10 listings for the same host and date yields exactly 1 persisted listing and 9 x 409 (DB unique index on (host_id, local_date)). Listing text runs the deterministic pre-filter; spam samples from the IT-03 labelled set are rejected or queued and never published. Malformed/oversized payloads are rejected by the validation layer with 422. Login rate limiting (NFR-05) blocks scripted credential cycling used to spin up posting accounts.
requirements.statusNote: DB unique index on (host_id, local_date) proven; the moderation half is wave 4, and the weekly cap carries the FR-11 ambiguity.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the (host_id, local_date) unique-index proof (10 concurrent creations -> exactly 1 row). The moderation half is wave 4 and the weekly cap carries the FR-11 ambiguity, so AB-03 stays PARTIAL.

requirements.text: Abusive content in chat or reviews: harassment, hate speech, or inappropriate content in messages (FR-06) or reviews (FR-05).
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Moderation Module, Safety Alert Service, Logging
requirements.acceptance: Abusive review text never becomes publicly visible: it is either rejected by the pre-filter or held pending and routed to the moderator queue. Abusive message text is delivered (per FR-08 policy) but asynchronously scanned; a flagged message is hidden from subsequent GETs and appears in the moderator queue. A moderator can escalate to a safety alert, and every moderation decision writes a MODERATION_DECISION row with category, outcome and decided_by (NFR-08). Offensive items from the >=200-item labelled set are detected within the <5% false-negative bound (IT-03).
requirements.statusNote: Depends on FR-05, FR-06 and FR-08, none of which exist.

reverification.mustProve: Depends on FR-05, FR-06 and FR-08, none of which exist. Report not_implemented.

requirements.text: Account takeover: credential stuffing or brute force against user accounts.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Authentication Service (hashing, rate limiting), Network Security Layer
requirements.acceptance: A scripted brute-force of 50 attempts against one account is locked out after 5 failures within 10 minutes (429 with Retry-After) and correct credentials are still refused during the lockout. Passwords are stored only as Argon2id/bcrypt hashes (ST-02) so a stolen dump yields no plaintext. All login traffic is HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ and plain HTTP is refused (ST-01). Session tokens are opaque, >= 128 bits of entropy, stored in Redis with a TTL, and delivered in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie; logout deletes the Redis session so the token is unusable afterwards.
requirements.statusNote: ST-02/ST-03/ST-01 + session-token entropy, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, logout invalidation.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute ST-01/ST-02/ST-03 plus session-token entropy, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie attributes and logout invalidation.

requirements.text: Injection attacks: SQL injection or XSS via search fields, listing text, chat, or reviews.
requirements.acceptance: The ST-04 payload suite (SQLi and XSS vectors) is fired at every input boundary — search query params, listing create/update text, chat messages, review comments, profile fields, moderation notes. Assertions: no request returns 500, no response contains unescaped payload markup, the users/listings/bookings tables are intact after the run, and no query is built by string concatenation (static grep). An OWASP ZAP baseline scan against the running app reports no high-risk alerts.
requirements.statusNote: Targeted SQLi/XSS suite passes; the OWASP ZAP baseline scan has a CI workflow and a documented procedure (STS-W3-04 fix) but has never been RUN, so no report exists.

reverification.mustProve: The targeted SQLi/XSS suite is re-executed. The OWASP ZAP baseline clause has a CI workflow and a documented procedure but has NEVER been run, so no report exists and AB-06 stays PARTIAL.

requirements.text: MEHKO evasion via duplicate accounts: a host creates multiple accounts to exceed the legal daily meal limit.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Registration/Email Verification, Listing Service (single enforcement point), Logging
requirements.acceptance: users.email carries a unique constraint; a second registration with the same email returns 409 and creates no row, and an account cannot publish until that email is verified (FR-10). The daily cap is enforced in exactly one server-side place (the listing service, backed by the DB unique index) — a grep proves no second implementation and no client-side-only check. Listing creations are logged with host ID and local date so duplicate-account patterns are reviewable (NFR-08). Phone-number uniqueness and identity verification are recorded as deferred to v2.0 and are explicitly not implemented.
requirements.statusNote: Unique verified email + single server-side daily enforcement point; multi-account evasion remains an accepted v1.0 residual per ADR-009.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the unique-verified-email proof (duplicate registration -> 409, no row) and the single server-side daily enforcement point grep. Multi-account evasion remains an accepted v1.0 residual per ADR-009.

requirements.text: Scraping of personal data: automated harvesting of host addresses and profiles.
requirements.designElement: Misuse cases (SRS §3.5) — Session authentication, Eligibility Policy, Data minimization in API responses
requirements.acceptance: Every profile, listing-detail, host-profile and messaging endpoint requires a valid session; unauthenticated requests get 401 and are never served personal data. Responses are built from explicit field allowlists: host email, phone, emergency contact and exact street address never appear in any list or detail payload (only approximate/geocoded area is exposed pre-booking; the precise address is released only to a confirmed guest of that booking). A test enumerates every public response schema and fails on any disallowed PII key. Read-API rate limiting is documented as an explicitly deferred v2.0 control and is not implemented. ADR-010: the public serializer is the DEFAULT on every read path, so a newly added endpoint is minimal unless it deliberately opts into the privileged view; the adr-conformance lane enumerates search, listing detail, host profile, messaging and moderation responses and fails on any exact address or precise coordinate outside the pending/in-progress-booking and moderator cases.
requirements.statusNote: Session-authenticated reads, allowlist serialisation, ADR-010 public-serializer sweep. COV-01 (flaky canary assertion) is the open item.

reverification.mustProve: Re-execute the ADR-010 public-serializer sweep over every read path. COV-01 (the canary that matched random UUIDs) appears already rewritten to leaf-scoped assertions on disk — confirm by execution and close it, or reopen it.

suiteDeterminism.diagnosisToConfirm: The stated hypothesis (jest runs suites in parallel workers) does NOT hold as written: jest.config.js pins maxWorkers: 1, so suites within one run are serial. The surviving mechanisms are (a) assertions that scan GLOBAL state — a whole-table SELECT or a whole-table row count — and therefore observe rows written by EARLIER suites in the same run, since the schema is reset only once in globalSetup and never between suites; (b) work that outlives the suite that started it (an unawaited request, an outbox worker tick, an open pg pool or Redis client) mutating shared state during a later suite — the same leak that keeps the process alive at the end. Confirm (b) with jest --detectOpenHandles before choosing a fix; if it holds, one root cause explains both PRIORITY 0 and PRIORITY 0b.
suiteDeterminism.rule: Fix the CAUSE: scope each assertion to rows and keys the test itself created, or make globally-scanning tests run serially/exclusively, and close the leaked handle. Never delete or weaken an assertion, never paper over it with retries or sleeps. Until 5 consecutive full-suite runs are identical and the process exits on its own, NO pass claim in this repository is worth anything and nothing is pushed.
